changes.now: Arthur Harrow smashes Ammit's ushabti at the pyramids of Giza, freeing the goddess to judge humanity and kill people for sins they have not yet committed.
changes.proposed: Arthur Harrow kills the avatars of the other gods at the pyramids of Giza and smashes Ammit's ushabti, freeing the goddess to judge humanity and kill people for sins they have not yet committed.
changes.evidence: In 'Gods and Monsters', Harrow kills the avatars of the Ennead's gods himself and then destroys Ammit's ushabti to free her; Ammit is not yet free when the avatars die. Wikipedia: 'Harrow kills the avatars of the other Egyptian gods and frees Ammit.' Fandom Ammit page: 'Arthur Harrow killed the Avatars of the Ennead Council and destroyed Ammit's ushabti.'

changes.now: Ammit kills the avatars of the other gods, and Harrow's followers spread through Cairo judging its people. Marc Spector and Steven Grant return from the Duat, Layla becomes Taweret's avatar, and Khonshu, freed from his ushabti, fights Ammit as a giant beside the pyramids, until Khonshu's and Taweret's avatars seal Ammit inside Harrow's body.
changes.proposed: Harrow's followers spread through Cairo judging its people. Marc Spector and Steven Grant return from the Duat, Layla becomes Taweret's avatar, and Khonshu, freed from his ushabti, fights Ammit as a giant beside the pyramids, until Khonshu's and Taweret's avatars seal Ammit inside Harrow's body.
changes.evidence: Harrow, not Ammit, kills the other gods' avatars, before Ammit is freed (that fact moves into the cause).

now: The avatars of the Ennead's gods, killed by Ammit.
proposed: The avatars of the Ennead's gods, killed by Harrow.
changes.evidence: Harrow kills the Ennead Council's avatars before he destroys Ammit's ushabti.
